The Company holds $3.1 billion of fixed maturity securities, of which approximately 62% are corporate bonds and 24% are structured product exposures including commercial mortgage backed securities and collateralized loan obligations. During the quarter, the Group increased its allocation to non-agency CMBS by $180 million to capture wider spreads. Investment yields averaged 4.95% on the portfolio, but the duration of 5.8 years leaves the book sensitive to a sustained 100 basis point rise in benchmark yields, which management estimates would reduce unrealized gains currently sitting at $87 million and could push the portfolio into a net unrealized loss position. The Company also maintains a $425 million revolving credit facility maturing in March of next year, with one financial covenant tied to subsidiary statutory surplus that becomes more restrictive if combined ratio exceeds 108% on a trailing four-quarter basis.

Billings performance in the quarter was influenced by the rollout of our new usage-based pricing module, which has been adopted by roughly 31% of new customers but only 9% of the installed base twelve months in. We view this as an early indicator that the legacy per-seat model still drives the majority of expansion revenue, and we have accordingly deferred $18 million of planned feature development into fiscal 2026 to focus engineering capacity on migration tooling. The Company relies on a single hyperscale cloud provider for approximately 78% of hosted customer workloads under a master services agreement that renews in November 2026. While the relationship has been stable, any material change in service credits, pricing or commitment terms at renewal could affect gross margin by an estimated 150 to 220 basis points. Management continues to evaluate multi-cloud abstractions but does not currently anticipate broad production deployment before the second half of next year.

Approximately 18% of our fiscal revenue was generated through our co-branded credit card program with a single external financial institution, and any reduction in the marketing support, reward funding, or underwriting standards provided by that partner could adversely affect the program's contribution to operating income. The agreement is subject to renewal in the third quarter of the next fiscal year, and the Company's ability to renegotiate favorable economic terms depends in part on the partner's then-current view of portfolio performance, prevailing interest rates, and the regulatory environment for consumer credit. Loss of, or a material deterioration in, the relationship could result in lower customer engagement and reduced data-driven marketing effectiveness.

Looking at the personal lines book, we are seeing average premium growth of about 9% year to date, mostly driven by rate adequacy in coastal homeowners. That said, I want to flag a concentration concern: roughly 38% of our dwelling fire and hurricane exposure sits in three Gulf states, and our largest single zip code now represents close to $90 million in insured value. A single major landfall event in that footprint would push our gross loss well past our panel reinsurance retention, and given that our tower covers only $1.4 billion per occurrence, the net earnings hit could be material even with reinstatement purchased. We continue to push non-renewals on properties valued over $4 million in those zip codes, but the pace has been slower than we targeted, and we have only completed about 60% of the planned actions through the third quarter.

Our grain handling and export business had a tough quarter, primarily because of issues at our sole deepwater loading terminal on the Pacific coast. A thirty day labour action by longshoremen slowed vessel turnaround, and we estimate we deferred approximately 140,000 tonnes of corn and soy shipments into the second half. We have since resumed loading, but two customers have already invoked force majeure clauses and we are in active dialogue with a third about deferred delivery penalties. The terminal itself represents nearly all of our bulk export capacity, and the Board is now reviewing options for redundancy, though no capital project is funded at this point. Separately, our Black Sea origination desk continues to operate under enhanced sanctions screening protocols, and we have declined four new counterparty relationships this quarter where ultimate beneficial ownership could not be satisfactorily established.

The Issuer is a vertically integrated specialty retailer of consumer electronics, with significant exposure to imported finished goods and component parts. Approximately 72% of merchandise cost is sourced from manufacturers located in the People's Republic of China, Vietnam and Taiwan, and a substantial portion of those goods is transported through the ports of Long Beach, California and Yantian prior to distribution to the Company's 620 stores and three regional fulfillment centers. The Company does not maintain long-term fixed-price supply contracts with respect to a majority of its inventory, and pricing is generally reset on a quarterly basis. As a result, the Company is exposed to (i) increased input costs as a result of tariffs, export controls or other trade measures imposed by the United States or foreign governments, (ii) delays or shortages arising from port congestion, labor actions, or geopolitical conflict in the Taiwan Strait or South China Sea, and (iii) the inability of certain key vendors, several of which are single-source for specific product categories, to fulfill purchase orders on acceptable terms. Any of these events could reduce gross margin, constrain inventory availability, and force the Company to raise retail prices, which may adversely affect customer demand.

The Company designs, manufactures and retails premium home furnishings through approximately 210 owned stores in the United States and Canada, an independent designer network, and a direct-to-consumer digital channel. A material portion of the Company's revenue is generated from a relatively narrow range of upholstery and case goods collections, the top five of which accounted for approximately 38% of net sales in the most recent fiscal year. The Company relies on a small number of domestic freight carriers for store replenishment and customer delivery, and on third-party carriers for inbound inventory from its manufacturing partners in Mexico and North Carolina. Any disruption in the availability of natural gas, certain chemicals used in finishing operations, or transportation services could result in delayed shipments, increased freight costs, or temporary closure of manufacturing facilities, which in turn could adversely affect the Company's ability to fulfill customer orders on a timely basis.

Turning to operational execution, our capex programme for the fiscal year remains on track at roughly 1.2 billion dollars, though we are seeing genuine pressure on a handful of large tunnelling contracts in the southern service territory. Two of our civil works partners have walked off the job citing unresolved commercial disputes, which has pushed the relevant main laying milestones into the back half of the year and triggered liquidated damages discussions on at least one municipal framework. We continue to engage with those counterparties and have activated backup contractors, but the resequencing is real. Separately, our non-household retail base represents about 11 percent of revenue, but a small group of industrial customers in chemicals and paper accounts for nearly 40 percent of that segment, so any single site closure or volume curtailment hits us disproportionately. On the regulatory front, the draft determination from our economic regulator still references a WACC range of 3.6 to 3.9 percent, materially below what we submitted at 4.5 percent, and we are weighing a formal reference. Finally, we are watching a proposed change to the abstraction licence regime that could raise our annual abstraction fees by an estimated 6 to 9 million pounds once enacted.

On July 22, the Company received notification from a former warehouse services customer that an arbitration demand had been filed with the American Arbitration Association seeking approximately $28.4 million in damages, plus interest and costs, arising from an alleged failure to maintain specified service level thresholds under a 2019 master services agreement covering three distribution centers in the southeastern United States. The claim principally asserts that throughput shortfalls during the fourth quarter of the prior fiscal year triggered contractual penalties and an early termination event. The Company believes the claim is without merit and intends to defend vigorously, while noting that discovery could reveal operational data that complicates a complete defense. Independent external counsel has been engaged and a reserve has been established in an amount that is not material to the consolidated financial statements, although this assessment may change as the proceeding advances. The matter is expected to remain pending for between eighteen and thirty months, during which management attention and incremental legal expense will be required.

The Group depends on a single deepwater tailings disposal facility at its flagship Colina Verde operation, which is permitted to accept approximately 28 million tonnes of tailings per annum. Any unplanned interruption to this facility, including structural failure of the containment dam, regulatory curtailment of discharge volumes, or extended power supply disruption affecting pumping infrastructure, would force a suspension of milling at the adjacent concentrator within seventy two hours. Tailings produced at the concentrator cannot be redirected to alternative storage without capital expenditure estimated at USD 85 million and an eighteen to twenty four month permitting and construction timetable. A multi month shutdown would defer between 65,000 and 90,000 tonnes of cathode output, materially reduce free cash flow for the affected period, and may attract enforcement action under the country's mining safety regulations, including potential suspension of the operating licence for the Colina Verde pit.

A significant share of the Group's research and development headcount is located in two engineering centers in Eastern Europe, and a portion of customer support operations is delivered from a nearshore facility in a jurisdiction that has in the past imposed temporary restrictions on cross-border data flows. Renewed geopolitical tension, expanded sanctions, or restrictions on the movement of personnel and capital could limit the Group's ability to recruit, retain, and redeploy technical staff in these locations. Any sustained disruption to productivity at these sites, or the need to relocate teams on compressed timelines, would likely increase compensation expense, delay product releases, and elevate the risk of unplanned downtime for hosted customers. The Group maintains limited redundant capacity for these functions and would need to rely on third-party staffing partners at premium pricing during any transition period.

In addition, certain open-source components embedded in the Group's flagship analytics platform are maintained by a small number of independent maintainers. If any of these maintainers cease to publish patches, including for newly disclosed vulnerabilities, or if their projects are relicensed on terms incompatible with the Group's distribution model, the Group may be required to undertake a costly fork, relicense dependent modules, or ship a product version with reduced functionality until alternatives are qualified. The Group does not maintain contractual service-level commitments with most of these maintainers, which limits its recourse if support is withdrawn.

The Group manufactures precision-machined transmission components and electric-drive subassemblies for OEM customers concentrated in Western Europe and North America. A material portion of consolidated revenue in the trailing twelve months was derived from three platform awards scheduled for volume ramp between 2025 and 2027, the largest of which represents approximately 24% of forward-looking production capacity booked under a take-or-pay framework. Cancellation or sustained deferral of any of these programs would result in immediate under-recovery of capitalized toolings, estimated at EUR 38 million in aggregate at the balance sheet date. Investors should further note that the Group's supply agreement with its primary silicon-carbide semiconductor supplier contains a fixed annual price escalator of 6.5% over a four-year term, with limited substitution rights during the contract window.
